for ViT-B/32 on CIFAR-10 and CLIP ViT-B/32 on ImageNet-1K. In the scatter plots, points are checkpoints, color encodes layer-wise compression. Bar plots depict the accuracy gain <math id="A4.F9.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta=\mathrm{Acc}{(\text{{FOLD} })}-\mathrm{Acc}{(\text{{MAG1} })}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>Acc</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">FOLD</mtext><mtext> </mtext></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>Acc</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">MAG1</mtext><mtext> </mtext></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta=\mathrm{Acc}{(\text{{FOLD} })}-\mathrm{Acc}{(\text{{MAG1} })}</annotation></semantics></math>, which remains positive and typically grows with compression, indicating that even under lightweight LayerNorm adaptation <span id="A4.F9.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">FOLD</span> retains a consistent advantage over pruning. The figure follows the same setup as Fig. <a href="#S3.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ 3 Experimental Results ‣ Cut Less, Fold More: Model Compressionthrough the Lens of Projection Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> in the main paper, but for <span id="A4.F9.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">MAG2</span>.

<section id="A4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.3 </span>ViT-B/32 on CIFAR-10</h3>

<div id="A4.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The 200 Vision Transformers (ViT) also from <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Andriushchenko et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, width=256, were trained on CIFAR-10, batch size 128, for 200 epochs with a cosine learning rate schedule and linear warmup. The main hyperparameters are summarized in Tab. <a href="#A4.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ D.3 ViT-B/32 on CIFAR-10 ‣ Appendix D Training Details ‣ Cut Less, Fold More: Model Compressionthrough the Lens of Projection Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>.
We made use of the maximum learning rate, the use of data augmentation, and the use of Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM) in our evaluations.
All other settings were fixed.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A4.T4" class="ltx_table">
<table id="A4.T4.2" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">
<thead class="ltx_thead">
<tr id="A4.T4.2.1" class="ltx_tr" style="--ltx-bg-color:#DCE6F1;">
<th id="A4.T4.2.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_th_row ltx_border_tt"><span id="A4.T4.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-bg-color:#DCE6F1;">Parameter</span></th>
<th id="A4.T4.2.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt"><span id="A4.T4.2.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-bg-color:#DCE6F1;">Values</span></th></tr>

</section>
<section id="A4.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.4 </span>CLIP ViT-B/32 on ImageNet-1K</h3>

<div id="A4.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">CLIP <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Radford et al., 2021</a>)</cite> models are known for the widespread use of CLIP features <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ramesh et al., 2022</a>)</cite>. We use the pool of models introduced by <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wortsman et al. (2022b)</a></cite>, who fine-tuned the CLIP ViT-B/32 architecture on ImageNet-1K multiple times using different randomly sampled training hyperparameters<span id="footnote8" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">8</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">8</sup>
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">8</span>
              
              
              
              
              
              
              
            Download link: <a href="https://github.com/mlfoundations/model-soups/releases/" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://github.com/mlfoundations/model-soups/releases/</a></span></span></span>. These hyperparameters include learning rate, number of training epochs, weight decay, label smoothing, and augmentation strategies, as stated in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wortsman et al., 2022b</a>)</cite>. The resulting collection of 72 fine-tuned models provides a strong basis for evaluating the performance of model folding compared to pruning on CLIP ViT architectures. All checkpoints were evaluated jointly in our study, without parameter-specific ablations.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.5 </span>LLaMA-60M on Colossal Clean Crawled Corpus (C4)</h3>

<div id="A4.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We train 36 LLaMA-family models <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">Touvron et al., 2023a</a>; <a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">Touvron et al., 2023b</a>)</cite> with 60M and 130M parameters on the Colossal Clean Crawled Corpus (C4) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">Raffel et al., 2020</a>)</cite> on a NVIDIA DGX Station A100 featuring eight NVIDIA A100 GPUs (each equipped with 80GB memory). The training time for a LLaMA-60M model is about 45 minutes. Tab. <a href="#A4.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ D.5 LLaMA-60M on Colossal Clean Crawled Corpus (C4) ‣ Appendix D Training Details ‣ Cut Less, Fold More: Model Compressionthrough the Lens of Projection Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> summarizes the fixed hyperparameters used to train LLaMA-60M and LLaMA-130M. The learning rate is linearly warmed up, followed by a cosine annealing schedule that decays to 10% of the initial value. We use the T5-base tokenizer <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">Raffel et al., 2023</a>)</cite> and AdamW optimizer, consistent with prior work <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">Glentis et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">Han et al., 2024</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>

</section>
<section id="A5" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix E </span>Extended Empirical Comparison of Folding and Pruning</h2>

<div id="A5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We provide additional experiments to complement the main results.
Fig. <a href="#A4.F8" title="Figure 8 ‣ D.1 ResNet18 on CIFAR-10 Training Setup with Adam and SGD ‣ Appendix D Training Details ‣ Cut Less, Fold More: Model Compressionthrough the Lens of Projection Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> mirrors the setup of Fig. <a href="#S2.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ 2.3 Folding Dominates Pruning ‣ 2 Unified Framework for Pruning and Folding ‣ Cut Less, Fold More: Model Compressionthrough the Lens of Projection Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> in the main paper, but replaces the L1 criterion for magnitude pruning with L2 (<span id="A5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">MAG2</span>).
Similarly, Fig. <a href="#A4.F9" title="Figure 9 ‣ D.2 PreActResNet18 on CIFAR-10 ‣ Appendix D Training Details ‣ Cut Less, Fold More: Model Compressionthrough the Lens of Projection Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>, Fig. <a href="#A4.F10" title="Figure 10 ‣ D.2 PreActResNet18 on CIFAR-10 ‣ Appendix D Training Details ‣ Cut Less, Fold More: Model Compressionthrough the Lens of Projection Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>, Fig. <a href="#A5.F11" title="Figure 11 ‣ Appendix E Extended Empirical Comparison of Folding and Pruning ‣ Cut Less, Fold More: Model Compressionthrough the Lens of Projection Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a>, and Fig. <a href="#A5.F12" title="Figure 12 ‣ Appendix E Extended Empirical Comparison of Folding and Pruning ‣ Cut Less, Fold More: Model Compressionthrough the Lens of Projection Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a> extend the corresponding figures in the main paper to other network architectures and to the L2 case. Across all comparisons, the qualitative picture remains the same: <span id="A5.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">FOLD</span> consistently matches or outperforms magnitude pruning, independent of the chosen norm.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We further include ablations to study the robustness of these findings with respect to training hyperparameters.
Fig. <a href="#A5.F13" title="Figure 13 ‣ Appendix E Extended Empirical Comparison of Folding and Pruning ‣ Cut Less, Fold More: Model Compressionthrough the Lens of Projection Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a>, Fig. <a href="#A5.F14" title="Figure 14 ‣ Appendix E Extended Empirical Comparison of Folding and Pruning ‣ Cut Less, Fold More: Model Compressionthrough the Lens of Projection Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">14</span></a>, and Fig. <a href="#A5.F15" title="Figure 15 ‣ Appendix E Extended Empirical Comparison of Folding and Pruning ‣ Cut Less, Fold More: Model Compressionthrough the Lens of Projection Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">15</span></a> report the effect of varying learning rate, SAM strength, and RandAugment, respectively.
Finally, Fig. <a href="#A5.F16" title="Figure 16 ‣ Appendix E Extended Empirical Comparison of Folding and Pruning ‣ Cut Less, Fold More: Model Compressionthrough the Lens of Projection Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">16</span></a> shows the influence of weight decay.
Taken together, these studies confirm that the relative advantage of <span id="A5.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">FOLD</span> is stable across different regularization strategies and training configurations.</p>
</div>

<section id="A6" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix F </span>Additional Analyses: Sharpness, Runtime, and LLMs</h2>

<div id="A6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Below we report additional evaluations. We extend our study by training and compressing 60M- and 130M-parameter LLaMA models on C4, and provide analyses of sharpness, and measure runtime overhead.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A6.T6" class="ltx_table">
<div id="A6.T6.2" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_center ltx_transformed_outer" style="width:345.0pt;height:121.6pt;vertical-align:-59.6pt;"><span class="ltx_transformed_inner" style="transform:translate(-152.8pt,53.8pt) scale(0.530330571155849,0.530330571155849) ;">
<table id="A6.T6.2.1" class="ltx_tabular ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">
<thead class="ltx_thead">
<tr id="A6.T6.2.1.1" class="ltx_tr" style="--ltx-bg-color:#DCE6F1;">

</span></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:90%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 6: </span><span id="A6.T6.11" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Evaluation of <span id="A6.T6.11.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">FOLD</span> and <span id="A6.T6.11.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">MAG2</span> on LLaMA-130M</span> (in addition to LLaMA-60M evaluations in Tab. <a href="#S3.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 3 Experimental Results ‣ Cut Less, Fold More: Model Compressionthrough the Lens of Projection Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>). We train and evaluate 18 LLaMA-family models with 130M parameters on C4 while varying max_lr, warmup steps, and weight decay. Columns show perplexity of the pretrained model (0% sparsity) and perplexity after structured magnitude pruning and folding with 20% and 50% sparsity in FFN blocks. For higher learning rates, especially for the settings with the best achieved performance in each sparsity category (underlined), <span id="A6.T6.12" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">FOLD</span> consistently outperforms <span id="A6.T6.13" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">MAG2</span> (bold).</figcaption>
</figure>

</figure>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 18: </span><span id="A6.F18.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Uncompressed model accuracy vs. performance difference <math id="A6.F18.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta\text{Accuracy}=\mathrm{Acc}{(\text{{FOLD} })}-\mathrm{Acc}{(\text{{MAG} })}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_bold">Accuracy</mtext></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>Acc</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">FOLD</mtext><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_bold"> </mtext></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>Acc</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">MAG</mtext><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_bold"> </mtext></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta\text{Accuracy}=\mathrm{Acc}{(\text{{FOLD} })}-\mathrm{Acc}{(\text{{MAG} })}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span> The same setup as in Fig. <a href="#S2.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ 2.3 Folding Dominates Pruning ‣ 2 Unified Framework for Pruning and Folding ‣ Cut Less, Fold More: Model Compressionthrough the Lens of Projection Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> and Fig. <a href="#A4.F8" title="Figure 8 ‣ D.1 ResNet18 on CIFAR-10 Training Setup with Adam and SGD ‣ Appendix D Training Details ‣ Cut Less, Fold More: Model Compressionthrough the Lens of Projection Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>.
<span id="A6.F18.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Top row:</span> <span id="A6.F18.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">MAG1</span>,
<span id="A6.F18.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Bottom row:</span> <span id="A6.F18.11" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">MAG2</span>. Model folding shows strong performance on models of different quality, with amplified effect on high-performing models (especially on ResNet18, SGD and ViT-B/32).</figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="A6.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.1 </span>Sharpness and Barrier Analysis</h3>

<div id="A6.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We compute sharpness following the implementation by <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Andriushchenko et al. (2023)</a></cite>.
Sharpness for CLIP is measured only on the final projection layer using <math id="A6.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sim" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∼</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim</annotation></semantics></math>1000 images, while for PreActResNets it is computed over the full model and dataset.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Sharpness increases with compression ratio for all methods and architectures (Fig. <a href="#A6.F19" title="Figure 19 ‣ F.1 Sharpness and Barrier Analysis ‣ Appendix F Additional Analyses: Sharpness, Runtime, and LLMs ‣ Cut Less, Fold More: Model Compressionthrough the Lens of Projection Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">19</span></a>), reaching a peak before stronger compression pushes the model out of its original basin and into a flatter, lower-capacity region. This rise–then–fall pattern appears consistently in both PreActResNet and CLIP models, see Fig. <a href="#A6.F19" title="Figure 19 ‣ F.1 Sharpness and Barrier Analysis ‣ Appendix F Additional Analyses: Sharpness, Runtime, and LLMs ‣ Cut Less, Fold More: Model Compressionthrough the Lens of Projection Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">19</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The correlation analysis in Fig. <a href="#A6.F20" title="Figure 20 ‣ F.1 Sharpness and Barrier Analysis ‣ Appendix F Additional Analyses: Sharpness, Runtime, and LLMs ‣ Cut Less, Fold More: Model Compressionthrough the Lens of Projection Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">20</span></a> further supports this interpretation. Across the 200 compressed ResNet18 models, 50 compressed PreActResNet18s and 72 compressed CLIP models, <span id="A6.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">FOLD</span> exhibits negative correlations between <math id="A6.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math>-sharpness and <math id="A6.SS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math>-accuracy (<math id="A6.SS1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta\mathrm{Accuracy}=\mathrm{Acc}(\text{{FOLD} })-\mathrm{Acc}(\text{{MAG} })" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>Accuracy</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>Acc</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">FOLD</mtext><mtext> </mtext></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>Acc</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">MAG</mtext><mtext> </mtext></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta\mathrm{Accuracy}=\mathrm{Acc}(\text{{FOLD} })-\mathrm{Acc}(\text{{MAG} })</annotation></semantics></math>). As shown in the scatter plots and correlation tables of Fig. <a href="#A6.F20" title="Figure 20 ‣ F.1 Sharpness and Barrier Analysis ‣ Appendix F Additional Analyses: Sharpness, Runtime, and LLMs ‣ Cut Less, Fold More: Model Compressionthrough the Lens of Projection Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">20</span></a>, larger reductions in sharpness under <span id="A6.SS1.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">FOLD</span> relative to <span id="A6.SS1.p3.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">MAG</span> are associated with larger accuracy gains. This relationship holds across the evaluated compression ratios, up to the point where one of the models leaves the original basin and sharpness becomes less informative.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">In addition to the global sharpness trends discussed above, Fig. <a href="#A6.F21" title="Figure 21 ‣ F.1 Sharpness and Barrier Analysis ‣ Appendix F Additional Analyses: Sharpness, Runtime, and LLMs ‣ Cut Less, Fold More: Model Compressionthrough the Lens of Projection Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">21</span></a> and Fig. <a href="#A6.F22" title="Figure 22 ‣ F.1 Sharpness and Barrier Analysis ‣ Appendix F Additional Analyses: Sharpness, Runtime, and LLMs ‣ Cut Less, Fold More: Model Compressionthrough the Lens of Projection Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">22</span></a> provide a more
fine-grained view of how training hyperparameters influence the relationship between <math id="A6.SS1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math>-sharpness and <math id="A6.SS1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math>-accuracy under compression. For Adam-trained ResNet models (Fig. <a href="#A6.F21" title="Figure 21 ‣ F.1 Sharpness and Barrier Analysis ‣ Appendix F Additional Analyses: Sharpness, Runtime, and LLMs ‣ Cut Less, Fold More: Model Compressionthrough the Lens of Projection Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">21</span></a>), the scatter plots reveal a strong and stable negative correlation: whenever
<span id="A6.SS1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">FOLD</span> produces lower sharpness than magnitude pruning, it also achieves higher accuracy across
almost all pruning ratios. The structure of the point clouds, especially at high learning rates, shows that Adam’s adaptive scaling can induce highly anisotropic sharpness profiles, which in turn amplify the divergence between the compression trajectories of <span id="A6.SS1.p4.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">FOLD</span> and <span id="A6.SS1.p4.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">MAG</span>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">In contrast, SGD-trained models (Fig. <a href="#A6.F22" title="Figure 22 ‣ F.1 Sharpness and Barrier Analysis ‣ Appendix F Additional Analyses: Sharpness, Runtime, and LLMs ‣ Cut Less, Fold More: Model Compressionthrough the Lens of Projection Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">22</span></a>) exhibit a weaker and more dispersed relationship
between <math id="A6.SS1.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math>-sharpness and <math id="A6.SS1.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math>-accuracy, consistent with the flatter and more isotropic minima typically found by SGD. Under SGD, <span id="A6.SS1.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">FOLD</span> often remains slightly flatter than
magnitude pruning even when <math id="A6.SS1.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math>-sharpness <math id="A6.SS1.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\approx 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≈</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx 0</annotation></semantics></math>, explaining why <span id="A6.SS1.p5.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">FOLD</span> maintains a mild yet
more weakly correlated accuracy advantage. The interaction with SAM and augmentation further differs across optimizers: SAM tightens the <math id="A6.SS1.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math>-sharpness distribution under SGD,
stabilizing the performance gap in favor of <span id="A6.SS1.p5.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">FOLD</span>, while RandAug tends primarily to reduce variance without introducing strong directional trends.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS1.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS1.p6.1" class="ltx_p">These results highlight that the predictive power of sharpness for pruning outcomes is
optimizer- and hyperparameter-dependent: sharpness differences are highly informative for Adam-trained networks but less so for SGD, even though <span id="A6.SS1.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">FOLD</span> consistently follows a smoother and less disruptive compression path than magnitude-based pruning in both regimes.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS1.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS1.p7.1" class="ltx_p">These findings align with recent work linking compression and landscape geometry. AdaSAP <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bair et al., 2024</a>)</cite> treats pruning as a sharpness-aware process, and <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al. (2025)</a></cite> show that feasible pruning ratios depend on intrinsic flatness. Our results support this perspective: compression initially increases sharpness as degrees of freedom are removed within the same basin, but stronger compression forces the model into a flatter basin with reduced curvature. <span id="A6.SS1.p7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">FOLD</span> follows this trajectory more smoothly, maintaining basin structure and yielding lower barriers than <span id="A6.SS1.p7.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">MAG</span>.</p>
</div>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 19: </span><span id="A6.F19.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Worst-case <math id="A6.F19.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{\infty}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{\infty}</annotation></semantics></math> sharpness as a function of compression ratio across architectures and pruning methods.</span>
Each subplot reports the sharpness distribution for independently trained models at three perturbation radii
<math id="A6.F19.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\rho=10^{-4},\,5\times 10^{-4},\,10^{-3})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mn> 5</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>,</mo><msup><mn> 10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\rho=10^{-4},\,5\times 10^{-4},\,10^{-3})</annotation></semantics></math>.
Panels (a)–(d) show <span id="A6.F19.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">FOLD</span> sharpness for ResNet18 trained with Adam and SGD, PreActResNet18, and CLIP ViT-B/32, respectively.
Panels (e)–(h) show the corresponding results for <span id="A6.F19.11" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">MAG1</span>.
Observed trends:
(i) Sharpness generally increases with compression ratio up to moderate levels before flattening or dropping at extreme compression.
(ii) <span id="A6.F19.12" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">FOLD</span> produces on-average lower sharpness than <span id="A6.F19.13" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">MAG1</span>.
(iii) Transformer models (CLIP ViT-B/32) experience substantially sharper solutions under compression compared to residual networks.
These patterns indicate that <span id="A6.F19.14" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">FOLD</span> maintains flatter loss landscapes across a wide range of settings, whereas <span id="A6.F19.15" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">MAG</span> more often drives models toward sharper and less stable minima.</figcaption>
</figure>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:90%;">CLIP ViT-B/32, 
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="A6.F20.fig4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">FOLD</span> vs <span id="A6.F20.fig4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">MAG1</span> </figcaption>
</figure></div></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 20: </span><span id="A6.F20.13" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Correlation between <math id="A6.F20.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math>-sharpness and <math id="A6.F20.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math>-accuracy across architectures and pruning baselines.</span>
Each column shows the relationship between pruning–induced differences in worst-case <math id="A6.F20.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{\infty}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{\infty}</annotation></semantics></math> sharpness
(<math id="A6.F20.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math> sharpness = <span id="A6.F20.14" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">FOLD</span> <math id="A6.F20.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="A6.F20.15" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">mag</span>) and differences in test accuracy (<math id="A6.F20.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math> accuracy = <span id="A6.F20.16" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">FOLD</span> <math id="A6.F20.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="A6.F20.17" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">mag</span>), for the pair of pruning methods indicated below each plot.
Color encodes the layer-wise compression ratio.
The tables underneath each subplot report Pearson and Spearman correlations at every compression ratio,
quantifying how predictive the sharpness difference is of the accuracy difference. Results are shown for <span id="A6.F20.18" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">FOLD</span> vs <span id="A6.F20.19" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">MAG1</span> for ResNet18 trained with Adam and SGD, PreActResNet18 and CLIP ViT-B/32. Statistics are computed over  200 independently trained ResNets18 and 50 PreActResNet18 on CIFAR-10, and 72 CLIP ViT-B/32 models on ImageNet-1K. Correlations use the sharpness value at <math id="A6.F20.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho=5\times 10^{-4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho=5\times 10^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math>. Results at <math id="A6.F20.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho=10^{-4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho=10^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A6.F20.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho=10^{-3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho=10^{-3}</annotation></semantics></math> are qualitatively very close.</figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="A6.F21" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1"><img src="2602.18116v1/fig/resnet/adam-fold-sharpness_adam-mag-l1-sharpness_delta_vs_delta_lr.png" id="A6.F21.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_figure_panel ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/127;" width="476" height="127" alt="Refer to caption"></div><div class="ltx_flex_break"></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1"><img src="2602.18116v1/fig/resnet/adam-fold-sharpness_adam-mag-l1-sharpness_delta_vs_delta_SAM.png" id="A6.F21.g2" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_figure_panel ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/127;" width="476" height="127" alt="Refer to caption"></div><div class="ltx_flex_break"></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1"><img src="2602.18116v1/fig/resnet/adam-fold-sharpness_adam-mag-l1-sharpness_delta_vs_delta_randaug.png" id="A6.F21.g3" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_figure_panel ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/127;" width="476" height="127" alt="Refer to caption"></div></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 21: </span><span id="A6.F21.15" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Sharpness-accuracy trade-off between <span id="A6.F21.15.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">FOLD</span> and <span id="A6.F21.15.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">MAG1</span> for ResNet18 trained with Adam.</span> Each column corresponds to a layer-wise compression ratio (0.1–0.9), and the three rows group models by learning rate, SAM configuration (including <math id="A6.F21.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ρ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho</annotation></semantics></math>), and RandAug usage. Points show <math id="A6.F21.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math> worst-case <math id="A6.F21.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{\infty}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{\infty}</annotation></semantics></math> sharpness (<span id="A6.F21.16" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">FOLD</span> <math id="A6.F21.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="A6.F21.17" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">MAG1</span>) vs. <math id="A6.F21.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math> test accuracy (<span id="A6.F21.18" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">FOLD</span> <math id="A6.F21.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="A6.F21.19" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">MAG1</span>).
<span id="A6.F21.20" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Observations:</span>
(1) The difference in model sharpness strongly predicts the difference in performance between <span id="A6.F21.21" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">FOLD</span> and <span id="A6.F21.22" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">MAG1</span> across almost all pruning ratios.
(2) <em id="A6.F21.23" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Learning rate:</em> higher learning rates lead to more dispersed sharpness changes. For models trained with Adam using high learning rates, <span id="A6.F21.24" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">MAG1</span> moves the model along a less sharp path compared to <span id="A6.F21.25" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">FOLD</span>, which struggles to catch up. However, the behavior flips for moderate and low learning rates.
(3) <em id="A6.F21.26" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">SAM/</em><math id="A6.F21.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ρ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho</annotation></semantics></math>: using SAM reduces the variability in the sharpness shift between methods, especially for larger <math id="A6.F21.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ρ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho</annotation></semantics></math>. <math id="A6.F21.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math> sharpness gets closer to zero.
(4) <em id="A6.F21.27" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">RandAug:</em> augmentation show little specific visible trend.</figcaption>
</figure>

<div class="ltx_flex_figure">

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 22: </span><span id="A6.F22.16" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Sharpness-accuracy trade-off between <span id="A6.F22.16.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">FOLD</span> and <span id="A6.F22.16.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">MAG1</span> for ResNet18 trained with SGD.</span>
Each column corresponds to a layer-wise compression ratio (0.1–0.9), and the three rows group models by learning rate, SAM configuration (including <math id="A6.F22.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ρ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho</annotation></semantics></math>), and RandAug usage.
Points show <math id="A6.F22.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math> worst-case <math id="A6.F22.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{\infty}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{\infty}</annotation></semantics></math> sharpness (<span id="A6.F22.17" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">FOLD</span> <math id="A6.F22.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="A6.F22.18" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">MAG1</span>) vs. <math id="A6.F22.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math> test accuracy (<span id="A6.F22.19" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">FOLD</span> <math id="A6.F22.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="A6.F22.20" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">MAG1</span>).
<span id="A6.F22.21" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Observations:</span>
(1) For SGD, the relationship between <math id="A6.F22.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math> sharpness and <math id="A6.F22.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math> accuracy is visibly weaker and more scattered than for Adam, reflecting the flatter and more anisotropic minima found by SGD.
(2) <em id="A6.F22.22" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Learning rate:</em> Unlike Adam, higher SGD learning rates do not systematically increase the sharpness gap between the methods. For most ratios, <span id="A6.F22.23" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">FOLD</span> tends to remain less sharp than <span id="A6.F22.24" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">MAG1</span>, producing positive <math id="A6.F22.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math> accuracy even when <math id="A6.F22.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math> sharpness is near zero.
(3) <em id="A6.F22.25" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">SAM/</em><math id="A6.F22.m25" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ρ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho</annotation></semantics></math>: SAM has a strong flattening effect under SGD—<math id="A6.F22.m26" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math> sharpness clusters tightly around zero, and the accuracy advantage of <span id="A6.F22.26" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">FOLD</span> becomes more stable as <math id="A6.F22.m27" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ρ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho</annotation></semantics></math> increases.
(4) <em id="A6.F22.27" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">RandAug:</em> Augmentation increases robustness to pruning under SGD, reducing the spread in <math id="A6.F22.m28" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math> accuracy and further weakening the sharpness–accuracy link. Overall, SGD-trained models exhibit a regime where <span id="A6.F22.28" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">FOLD</span> consistently follows a gentler sharpness trajectory than <span id="A6.F22.29" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">MAG1</span>, leading to a clearer accuracy advantage at moderate pruning ratios.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.2 </span>Runtime overhead and equivalence of compressed models</h3>

<div id="A6.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We profile both the compression procedures and the inference behavior of the resulting compressed models on a dedicated DGX A100 server equipped with dual-socket AMD EPYC 7742 CPUs (256 hardware threads) and 8× NVIDIA A100 80GB GPUs. All measurements use the <span id="A6.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">THOP</span> profiler<span id="footnote9" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">9</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">9</sup>
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">9</span>
              
              
              
              
              
              
              
            <a href="https://github.com/ultralytics/thop" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://github.com/ultralytics/thop</a></span></span></span> and report compression time, peak memory during compression, per-batch latency, FLOPs, and peak forward-pass memory before and after compression.
For each architecture (PreActResNet18 and CLIP ViT-B/32), all compression methods generate the <em id="A6.SS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">same</em> compressed network topology (identical channel counts and tensor shapes). Consequently, all methods yield identical FLOPs and nearly identical latencies, demonstrating that inference-time behavior is determined entirely by the resulting architecture, not by the choice of compression algorithm. <span id="A6.SS2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">FOLD</span> introduces a moderate one-off compression overhead, but its inference-time profile matches the other compressed models.</p>
</div>

<td id="A6.T8.2.1.4.8" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_bb">637.88</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</span></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 8: </span>Runtime characteristics of CLIP ViT-B/32 before and after compression (<math id="A6.T8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="7.47\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>7.47</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7.47\%</annotation></semantics></math> parameter reduction). Latency is measured for a full batch. FLOPs are reported per image. Comp. time and Comp. peak mem refer to the one-off overhead of running the compression method.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A6.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A6.T8" title="Table 8 ‣ F.2 Runtime overhead and equivalence of compressed models ‣ Appendix F Additional Analyses: Sharpness, Runtime, and LLMs ‣ Cut Less, Fold More: Model Compressionthrough the Lens of Projection Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> shows the same evaluation for
CLIP ViT-B/32, where FFN blocks are compressed to with 20% layer-wise compression ratio. Here, FLOPs decrease from <math id="A6.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2946.76" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2946.76</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2946.76</annotation></semantics></math> MFLOPs/image to
<math id="A6.SS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2379.98" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2379.98</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2379.98</annotation></semantics></math> MFLOPs/image (a <math id="A6.SS2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="19.2\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>19.2</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">19.2\%</annotation></semantics></math> reduction), and latency improves
from <math id="A6.SS2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="19.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>19.8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">19.8</annotation></semantics></math> ms/batch to roughly <math id="A6.SS2.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="17.35" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>17.35</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">17.35</annotation></semantics></math> ms/batch
(about <math id="A6.SS2.p3.m6" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.14\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.14</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.14\times</annotation></semantics></math> speed-up). Again, <span id="A6.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">FOLD</span> is the slowest method due to its iterative nature to compute <math id="A6.SS2.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>-means clusters, but the compressed models share the same FLOPs, memory and latency.</p>
</div>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 9: </span>Per-layer comparison of PreActResNet18 after <span id="A6.T9.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">FOLD</span> and <span id="A6.T9.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">MAG2</span> at compression ratio <math id="A6.T9.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.4</annotation></semantics></math>. For each convolutional and linear layer we report parameters, per-image FLOPs, activation size, and the number of non-zero activations (effective activations). All per-layer differences are zero, confirming that parameters, FLOPs, activations, and effective activations are exactly matched between the two compressed models.</figcaption>
