<td id="A6.T10.2.1.76.12" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t">1972632</td>
<td id="A6.T10.2.1.76.13" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t">0</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</span></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 10: </span><span id="A6.T10.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Per-layer comparison of CLIP ViT-B/32 after <span id="A6.T10.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">FOLD</span> and <span id="A6.T10.4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">MAG2</span> at compression ratio <math id="A6.T10.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.2</annotation></semantics></math> (global parameter reduction <math id="A6.T10.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="7.47\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>7.47</mn><mo mathsize="1.110em">%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7.47\%</annotation></semantics></math>). The table reports all convolutional and linear layers in the vision transformer and classification head, including their parameters, per-image FLOPs, activation sizes, and effective activations.
The <span id="A6.T10.4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">transformer.resblocks.*</span> modules belong to CLIP’s text encoder. Because the ImageNet-1k fine-tuned variant evaluates only the vision encoder and classification head, the text encoder is not part of the forward graph. <span id="A6.T10.4.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">THOP</span> therefore records zero FLOPs and zero activations for these layers, while their parameters remain included in the model.
Note that the per-layer totals (<math id="A6.T10.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\approx 8.36\times 10^{7}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≈</mo><mrow><mn>8.36</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>7</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx 8.36\times 10^{7}</annotation></semantics></math> parameters) are smaller than the full model parameter count (<math id="A6.T10.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\approx 1.40\times 10^{8}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≈</mo><mrow><mn>1.40</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>8</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx 1.40\times 10^{8}</annotation></semantics></math>) because this table excludes components without FLOPs, such as token embeddings, positional embeddings, and LayerNorm parameters, which are included in the global counts but not part of the per-layer FLOP/activation analysis.
Several projection layers inside the attention blocks show zero FLOPs because CLIP implements attention using fused operations; these operations are profiled at the block level by <span id="A6.T10.4.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">THOP</span> rather than attributed to the individual Linear submodules.
All per-layer differences are zero, showing that <span id="A6.T10.4.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">FOLD</span> and <span id="A6.T10.4.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">MAG2</span> produce structurally identical compressed models on every layer affected by compression.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.3 </span>Impact of one rank slack and singleton folding</h3>

<div id="A6.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section we separate two effects in our pruning vs. folding comparison: (i) the influence of the one-rank slack in
Theorems <a href="#S2.Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 2.1. ‣ 2.3 Folding Dominates Pruning ‣ 2 Unified Framework for Pruning and Folding ‣ Cut Less, Fold More: Model Compressionthrough the Lens of Projection Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.1</span></a>–<a href="#S2.Thmtheorem2" title="Theorem 2.2. ‣ 2.3 Folding Dominates Pruning ‣ 2 Unified Framework for Pruning and Folding ‣ Cut Less, Fold More: Model Compressionthrough the Lens of Projection Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.2</span></a>, and
(ii) the intrinsic difference between pruning and folding as projection operators. We therefore contrast the gain from increasing the pruning rank from <math id="A6.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A6.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k{+}1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k{+}1</annotation></semantics></math> (blue curves in Fig. <a href="#A6.F23" title="Figure 23 ‣ F.3 Impact of one rank slack and singleton folding ‣ Appendix F Additional Analyses: Sharpness, Runtime, and LLMs ‣ Cut Less, Fold More: Model Compressionthrough the Lens of Projection Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">23</span></a>) with the gain from replacing pruning by folding at the same nominal rank (orange curves).
This isolates the contribution of rank from the contribution of the projection geometry.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Fig. <a href="#A6.F23" title="Figure 23 ‣ F.3 Impact of one rank slack and singleton folding ‣ Appendix F Additional Analyses: Sharpness, Runtime, and LLMs ‣ Cut Less, Fold More: Model Compressionthrough the Lens of Projection Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">23</span></a> shows both effects:
for each weight matrix <math id="A6.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐖</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}</annotation></semantics></math> (in every layer of ViT or ResNet18), it plots the relative Frobenius error change when the retained rank increases by one (blue) versus when the method changes from pruning to folding at fixed rank (orange), as a function of <math id="A6.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<table id="A6.Ex15" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.Ex15.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{\text{rank}}(k)\;=\;\frac{\|\mathbf{W}-\mathbf{W}_{p}^{(k)}\|_{F}\;-\;\|\mathbf{W}-\mathbf{W}_{p}^{(k+1)}\|_{F}}{\|\mathbf{W}\|_{F}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mtext>rank</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo rspace="0.280em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>𝐖</mi><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>F</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.502em" rspace="0.502em">−</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>𝐖</mi><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>F</mi></msub></mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝐖</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>F</mi></msub></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{\text{rank}}(k)\;=\;\frac{\|\mathbf{W}-\mathbf{W}_{p}^{(k)}\|_{F}\;-\;\|\mathbf{W}-\mathbf{W}_{p}^{(k+1)}\|_{F}}{\|\mathbf{W}\|_{F}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">This quantity measures the improvement obtained when increasing the retained rank from <math id="A6.SS3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A6.SS3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k+1</annotation></semantics></math> within magnitude pruning <span id="A6.SS3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">MAG2</span>. It isolates the rank slack effect. Across all examined layers, the improvement from a single additional retained channel is small, especially in deeper layers.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<table id="A6.Ex16" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.Ex16.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{\text{method}}(k)\;=\;\frac{\|\mathbf{W}-\mathbf{W}_{p}^{(k)}\|_{F}\;-\;\|\mathbf{W}-\mathbf{W}^{\star(k)}_{f}\|_{F}}{\|\mathbf{W}\|_{F}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mtext>method</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo rspace="0.280em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>𝐖</mi><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>F</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.502em" rspace="0.502em">−</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>𝐖</mi><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>f</mi><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋆</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>F</mi></msub></mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝐖</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>F</mi></msub></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{\text{method}}(k)\;=\;\frac{\|\mathbf{W}-\mathbf{W}_{p}^{(k)}\|_{F}\;-\;\|\mathbf{W}-\mathbf{W}^{\star(k)}_{f}\|_{F}}{\|\mathbf{W}\|_{F}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.SS3.p4.1" class="ltx_p">This measures the gain obtained by switching from structured magnitude pruning to optimal folding at the same rank <math id="A6.SS3.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>. The improvements are one to two orders of magnitude larger than the corresponding <math id="A6.SS3.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{\text{rank}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mtext>rank</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{\text{rank}}</annotation></semantics></math> values for nearly all layers.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS3.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS3.p5.1" class="ltx_p">The results empirically support the clarification presented in the rebuttal: although Theorems <a href="#S2.Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 2.1. ‣ 2.3 Folding Dominates Pruning ‣ 2 Unified Framework for Pruning and Folding ‣ Cut Less, Fold More: Model Compressionthrough the Lens of Projection Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.1</span></a>-<a href="#S2.Thmtheorem2" title="Theorem 2.2. ‣ 2.3 Folding Dominates Pruning ‣ 2 Unified Framework for Pruning and Folding ‣ Cut Less, Fold More: Model Compressionthrough the Lens of Projection Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.2</span></a> compare pruning at rank <math id="A6.SS3.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> to folding at rank <math id="A6.SS3.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k{+}1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k{+}1</annotation></semantics></math>, the contribution of the rank difference is negligible in practice. The blue curves show that <math id="A6.SS3.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\mathbf{W}-\mathbf{W}_{p}^{(k)}\|_{F}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>𝐖</mi><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>F</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\mathbf{W}-\mathbf{W}_{p}^{(k)}\|_{F}</annotation></semantics></math> changes only minimally when <math id="A6.SS3.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k\!\to\!k{+}1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0.108em" rspace="0.108em" stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k\!\to\!k{+}1</annotation></semantics></math>, while the orange curves demonstrate that folding provides a substantially tighter approximation than pruning at comparable compression levels. This confirms that the practical advantage of folding arises primarily from the richer family of cluster-based projections rather than the added rank.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A6.F23" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1"><img src="2602.18116v1/fig/resnet/adam_error_vs_rank.png" id="A6.F23.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_figure_panel ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:419/335;" width="419" height="335" alt="Refer to caption"></div><div class="ltx_flex_break"></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1"><img src="2602.18116v1/fig/vit/vit_error_vs_rank.png" id="A6.F23.g2" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_figure_panel ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:324/243;" width="324" height="243" alt="Refer to caption"></div></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 23: </span><span id="A6.F23.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Effect of increasing the retained rank by one is significantly lower than changing the compression method from <span id="A6.F23.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">MAG</span> to <span id="A6.F23.3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">FOLD</span>.<span id="A6.F23.3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Comparison of (i) the effect of increasing the retained rank by one (blue curves) and (ii) the effect of switching from <span id="A6.F23.3.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">MAG2</span> to <span id="A6.F23.3.3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">FOLD</span> at the same nominal rank (orange curves). Each panel corresponds to a single weight matrix <math id="A6.F23.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐖</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}</annotation></semantics></math> in ResNet18 convolutional layers (</span>top<span id="A6.F23.3.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">) and ViT-B/32 FFN layers (</span>bottom<span id="A6.F23.3.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">) and shows the relative Frobenius error difference <math id="A6.F23.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math> as a function of the retained rank <math id="A6.F23.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A6.SS3.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS3.p6.1" class="ltx_p">Fig. <a href="#A6.F24" title="Figure 24 ‣ F.3 Impact of one rank slack and singleton folding ‣ Appendix F Additional Analyses: Sharpness, Runtime, and LLMs ‣ Cut Less, Fold More: Model Compressionthrough the Lens of Projection Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">24</span></a> reports the relative squared error for pruning, special folding <math id="A6.SS3.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{f}^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>f</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{f}^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math>, and optimal folding <math id="A6.SS3.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{f}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>f</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{f}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> across all layers of ResNet18 and ViT-B/32 on CIFAR10, evaluated at multiple keep ratios. Three consistent phenomena appear:</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS3.p7" class="ltx_para">
<ul id="A6.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A6.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A6.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Pruning always yields the largest error.</span>
For every layer and every keep ratio, the pruning curves lie above both folding curves. This confirms empirically that pruning introduces the largest distortion of the original weight matrix.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A6.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A6.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Special folding <math id="A6.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{f}^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>f</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{f}^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> strictly improves over pruning.</span>
The construction used in Theorem <a href="#S2.Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 2.1. ‣ 2.3 Folding Dominates Pruning ‣ 2 Unified Framework for Pruning and Folding ‣ Cut Less, Fold More: Model Compressionthrough the Lens of Projection Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.1</span></a>, obtained by merging all pruned rows, leads to smaller reconstruction error for all layers and all keep ratios. This empirically validates the first inequality <math id="A6.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{error}(\mathbf{W}_{p})\geq\mathrm{error}(\mathbf{W}_{f}^{\prime})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>error</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mrow><mi>error</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>f</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{error}(\mathbf{W}_{p})\geq\mathrm{error}(\mathbf{W}_{f}^{\prime})</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A6.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A6.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Optimal folding <math id="A6.I1.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{f}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>f</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{f}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> achieves the smallest error.</span>
The <math id="A6.I1.i3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>-means solution consistently attains the lowest error, verifying the second inequality <math id="A6.I1.i3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{error}(\mathbf{W}_{f}^{\prime})\geq\mathrm{error}(\mathbf{W}_{f}^{*})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>error</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>f</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mrow><mi>error</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>f</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{error}(\mathbf{W}_{f}^{\prime})\geq\mathrm{error}(\mathbf{W}_{f}^{*})</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS3.p8" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS3.p8.1" class="ltx_p">Importantly, the gap between pruning and both folding methods is
larger than the very small difference induced by adding
a single additional cluster (<em id="A6.SS3.p8.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">i.e.</em>, increasing the rank from <math id="A6.SS3.p8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A6.SS3.p8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k+1</annotation></semantics></math>). This supports the clarification made in the rebuttal:
the practical advantage of folding does not stem from the <math id="A6.SS3.p8.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+1</annotation></semantics></math> change in rank, but from the richer family of cluster-based projections that folding can realize.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS3.p9" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS3.p9.1" class="ltx_p">The observed ordering, <em id="A6.SS3.p9.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">i.e.</em>, <math id="A6.SS3.p9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{error}(\mathbf{W}_{p})&gt;\mathrm{error}(\mathbf{W}_{f}^{\prime})&gt;\mathrm{error}(\mathbf{W}_{f}^{*})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>error</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><mi>error</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>f</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><mi>error</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>f</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{error}(\mathbf{W}_{p})&gt;\mathrm{error}(\mathbf{W}_{f}^{\prime})&gt;\mathrm{error}(\mathbf{W}_{f}^{*})</annotation></semantics></math>, holds uniformly across all layers of ResNet18 as well as FFN layers of ViT-B/32. This indicates that the theoretical inequalities are not only valid in principle but also manifest strongly and consistently in real trained models.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A6.F24" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1"><img src="2602.18116v1/fig/resnet/adam_special_vs_optimal.png" id="A6.F24.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_figure_panel ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:405/324;" width="405" height="324" alt="Refer to caption"></div><div class="ltx_flex_break"></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1"><img src="2602.18116v1/fig/vit/vit_special_vs_optimal.png" id="A6.F24.g2" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_figure_panel ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:310/232;" width="310" height="232" alt="Refer to caption"></div></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 24: </span><span id="A6.F24.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Relative reconstruction error of pruning, special folding <math id="A6.F24.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{f}^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>f</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{f}^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> (from the proof of Theorem <a href="#S2.Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 2.1. ‣ 2.3 Folding Dominates Pruning ‣ 2 Unified Framework for Pruning and Folding ‣ Cut Less, Fold More: Model Compressionthrough the Lens of Projection Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.1</span></a>), and optimal folding <math id="A6.F24.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{f}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>f</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{f}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> for all layers of ResNet18 (top) and ViT-B/32 (bottom).<span id="A6.F24.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
For each layer, we report the normalized squared Frobenius error <math id="A6.F24.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\mathbf{W}-\mathbf{W}_{\bullet}\|_{F}^{2}/\|\mathbf{W}\|_{F}^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>𝐖</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mo>∙</mo></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>F</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>/</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝐖</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>F</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\mathbf{W}-\mathbf{W}_{\bullet}\|_{F}^{2}/\|\mathbf{W}\|_{F}^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> at several keep ratios <math id="A6.F24.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k_{p}/m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo>/</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k_{p}/m</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A6.F24.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bullet\in\{\texttt{MAG2},\text{singleton},\texttt{FOLD}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">∙</mo><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.110em" minsize="1.110em">{</mo><mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">MAG2</mtext><mo>,</mo><mtext>singleton</mtext><mo>,</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">FOLD</mtext></mrow><mo maxsize="1.110em" minsize="1.110em">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bullet\in\{\texttt{MAG2},\text{singleton},\texttt{FOLD}\}</annotation></semantics></math>. <span id="A6.F24.3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">MAG2</span> (blue) denotes structured magnitude pruning with <math id="A6.F24.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k_{p}</annotation></semantics></math> retained rows. The special fold <math id="A6.F24.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{f}^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>f</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{f}^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> (orange) merges all pruned rows into a single extra cluster (<math id="A6.F24.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k_{f}=k_{p}+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>f</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k_{f}=k_{p}+1</annotation></semantics></math>). The optimal fold <math id="A6.F24.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{f}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>f</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{f}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> (green) is the <math id="A6.F24.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>-means solution with <math id="A6.F24.m25" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k_{f}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>f</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k_{f}</annotation></semantics></math> clusters.
Across all layers, <math id="A6.F24.m26" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{f}^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>f</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{f}^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> consistently outperforms pruning, and <math id="A6.F24.m27" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{f}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>f</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{f}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> yields the smallest error, empirically validating <math id="A6.F24.m28" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{error}(\mathbf{W}_{p})\geq\mathrm{error}(\mathbf{W}_{f}^{\prime})\geq\mathrm{error}(\mathbf{W}_{f}^{*})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>error</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mrow><mi>error</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>f</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mrow><mi>error</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>f</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{error}(\mathbf{W}_{p})\geq\mathrm{error}(\mathbf{W}_{f}^{\prime})\geq\mathrm{error}(\mathbf{W}_{f}^{*})</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A6.SS3.p10" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS3.p10.1" class="ltx_p">Across all layers of ResNet18 and ViT-B/32, the gain from increasing the retained rank by one is consistently negligible, while the gain from replacing pruning with folding is one to two orders of
magnitude larger (Fig. <a href="#A6.F23" title="Figure 23 ‣ F.3 Impact of one rank slack and singleton folding ‣ Appendix F Additional Analyses: Sharpness, Runtime, and LLMs ‣ Cut Less, Fold More: Model Compressionthrough the Lens of Projection Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">23</span></a>). Thus, the empirical advantage of folding is not a byproduct of the <math id="A6.SS3.p10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k\mapsto k{+}1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">↦</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k\mapsto k{+}1</annotation></semantics></math> rank slack, but stems from the richer family of cluster-based projections that folding can realize. This is further corroborated by the layer-wise reconstruction errors in Fig. <a href="#A6.F24" title="Figure 24 ‣ F.3 Impact of one rank slack and singleton folding ‣ Appendix F Additional Analyses: Sharpness, Runtime, and LLMs ‣ Cut Less, Fold More: Model Compressionthrough the Lens of Projection Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">24</span></a>, where
<math id="A6.SS3.p10.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{error}(\mathbf{W}_{p})&gt;\mathrm{error}(\mathbf{W}_{f}^{\prime})&gt;\mathrm{error}(\mathbf{W}_{f}^{*})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>error</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><mi>error</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>f</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><mi>error</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>f</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{error}(\mathbf{W}_{p})&gt;\mathrm{error}(\mathbf{W}_{f}^{\prime})&gt;\mathrm{error}(\mathbf{W}_{f}^{*})</annotation></semantics></math> holds uniformly. These results confirm that folding’s superior approximation properties are structural rather than an artifact of rank.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS3.p11" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS3.p11.1" class="ltx_p">The theory controls the loss via the parameter-Lipschitz bound
<math id="A6.SS3.p11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|L(\mathbf{W})-L(\mathbf{W}_{\bullet})|\leq\kappa\|\mathbf{W}-\mathbf{W}_{\bullet}\|_{F}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐖</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mo>∙</mo></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>𝐖</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mo>∙</mo></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>F</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|L(\mathbf{W})-L(\mathbf{W}_{\bullet})|\leq\kappa\|\mathbf{W}-\mathbf{W}_{\bullet}\|_{F}</annotation></semantics></math>. In regimes where <math id="A6.SS3.p11.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math> is moderate, <em id="A6.SS3.p11.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">e.g.</em>, flat solutions obtained with smaller learning rates or SAM-folding’s smaller Frobenius error reliably translates into smaller loss degradation. However, in sharp minima such as those produced by Adam at large learning rates (see Fig. <a href="#A6.F21" title="Figure 21 ‣ F.1 Sharpness and Barrier Analysis ‣ Appendix F Additional Analyses: Sharpness, Runtime, and LLMs ‣ Cut Less, Fold More: Model Compressionthrough the Lens of Projection Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">21</span></a> and Fig. <a href="#A6.F22" title="Figure 22 ‣ F.1 Sharpness and Barrier Analysis ‣ Appendix F Additional Analyses: Sharpness, Runtime, and LLMs ‣ Cut Less, Fold More: Model Compressionthrough the Lens of Projection Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">22</span></a>), the effective local <math id="A6.SS3.p11.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math> becomes extremely large. In this setting, even tiny parameter perturbations cause large loss changes, and the ordering of
Frobenius errors no longer predicts the ordering of accuracies. Thus, the discovered failure cases of folding are not contradictions of the theory but instances where the Lipschitz assumption required for loss control breaks down due to extreme curvature.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A7" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix G </span>Use of Large Language Models</h2>

<div id="A7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We used ChatGPT <span id="footnote10" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">10</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">10</sup>
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">10</span>
            
            
            
            
            
            
            
          ChatGPT / GPT-5: <a href="https://chatgpt.com" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://chatgpt.com</a></span></span></span> for sentence-level grammar correction and improvement, drafting trivial plotting snippets to produce figures from logs, and code readability edits. All ideas, proofs, experiments, and analyses are ours.</p>
</div>
</section><div class="ltx_rdf" about="" property="dcterms:creator"></div>
